newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU and Japan settle liquor tax differences.
newsitem.headline: EU and Japan settle liquor tax differences.

text.p: The European Union and Japan have settled a long-running dispute over Japanese tax on European liquor exports, the EU's executive said on Tuesday.
Japanese taxes on imports of European brown and white spirits will be slashed while tax on spirits produced in Japan will be raised, the European Commission said.
The changes will be introduced in two stages with the first on October 1, 1997, and the second a year later, the Commission said.
The EU and Japan have been at odds for years over the tax applied to European liquor exports.
Brown spirits, including cognac and whisky, are currently taxed at up to 600 percent higher than domestic products. This would be brought to within three percent.
White spirits, including vodka and gin, are currently taxed 250 percent higher than domestic products. The differences here would be scrapped.
The Commission said Japan would raise taxes on domestically produced spirits from October 1 as part of the deal.
Tax on so-called Shochu A spirit would be raised to 8,076 yen per kilolitre from 6,228 on October 1 and to 9,924 a year later.
Tax on Shochu B, currently at 4,084 yen per kilolitre would be raised to 6,028 on October 1, to 7,976 a year later and to 9,924 in 2001.
Japanese tax on imports of brown spirits -- which include whisky and brandy -- will be slashed from 24,558 yen per kilolitre to 13,775 in October and 10,225 a year later.
Tax on imports of white spirits such as vodka and gin will be cut to 9,924 yen in October from 9,927, while tax on liqueurs will be raised to 9,924 from 8,217 at the same time.
